title: pr-100777-instrument-invocation-onset-latency-and-token-cost-derivation.json
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Users and SRE teams have asked for deterministic attribution of early invocation latency (onset) and its token-level cost implications; long-tail spikes at sequence start have caused noisy SLOs and opaque billing variance. This PR introduces a lightweight onset-latency meter combined with a derived token-cost estimator and a compact dashboard to make early-invocation behavior actionable. Scope: implement a server-side 'invocation_onset' metric that captures the time from request receipt to first model token emission, instrument token-level cost derivation for the first N tokens with hardware and quantization tags, surface aggregated histograms and P95/P99 onset + token-cost correlations, and add a dashboard + alert tuning recipe. Design summary: 1) invocation_onset counter/histogram emitted as OTLP metric with labels: model, variant, region, tenant_tier, sequence_shape, and hw_quant_profile; 2) first_tokens_cost gauge series derived by multiplying per-token hardware cost weights by token durations for tokens 0..N-1, emitted as a per-invocation histogram sample for downstream rollups; 3) a small sampling layer that captures full spans for 1% of invocations flagged as high-onset to reduce trace volume; 4) a dashboard JSON with aggregated panels (onset distribution, first-token cost scatter, onset vs. model latency heatmap) and a recommended alert rule that uses a composite of onset P95 > threshold AND first_tokens_cost P90 delta to reduce noisy alerts. Checklist: - [x] metric schema defined and stable - [x] OTLP exporter hook added in runtime pipeline - [x] derived token-cost estimator implemented with configurable N (default 8) - [x] dashboard JSON included and linked to the Observability catalog - [x] unit + e2e tests for metric emission and derivation - [x] documentation page with rollout/alert tuning guidance - [x] 10% canary rollout plan in release notes Performance/backwards compatibility: metrics are additive; the added histogram buckets are compact and default to disabled high-fidelity sampling. Default rollout keeps sampling at 0.1% for full spans and derived metrics only emit lightweight histogram aggregates to existing metric backends. Testing: unit tests cover the estimator math across quantization profiles and simulated kernel timings; e2e bench reproduces spike scenarios and validates alert suppression logic. CI: initial lint caught a formatting issue which was fixed; full pipeline passed on final run. Rollout: staged canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) over 48 hours with monitoring for metric ingestion lag. Related: ties to ENG-4762 (onset SLO decomposition) and PM-312 (dashboard requirements).

review_comments: 2026-03-02 - Liam Carter: Nice work — can we ensure the hw_quant_profile label cardinality stays bounded? Suggest mapping to a small set of enums instead of raw strings.
2026-03-02 - Maya Chen (author): Agreed. Added a normalization table that maps quant profiles to four enums (fp32, int8, q4, q5_1). Updated metric emission to use the enum key.
2026-03-03 - Noah Patel: The sampling rate knob should be configurable via environment/console and default to 0.1% in hosted. Also add a debug flag to force full capture for single-tenants.
2026-03-03 - Maya Chen (author): Added OBS_ONSET_FULL_SAMPLING_PERCENT env var and tenant_override flag. Docs updated with examples.
2026-03-04 - Zoe Kim: Alert recipe looks good but recommend using a sliding window of 10m with at least 50 invocations to avoid weekend noise. Also request unit test for the alert payload builder.
2026-03-04 - Maya Chen (author): Added alert window change, added unit test for alert builder and included guidance in the docs for threshold calibration.
release_notes: Added invocation_onset metrics and derived first_tokens_cost estimator. New dashboard: Onset Latency & First-Tokens Cost. New alert recipe: composite onset + token-cost regression to reduce noisy alerts. Rollout: staged canary; sampling disabled by default for hosted accounts below enterprise tier.
testing_summary: Unit tests (metric schema, estimator math) and e2e stability bench included. CI pipeline green on final run. Local stress run shows <0.5% CPU overhead when emitting histograms at default sampling; canary validated ingestion and alert suppression behavior.
canary_plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with metric ingestion and alert noise monitoring; rollback if ingestion lag >= 2m or alert rate increases >30%.
notes_for_ops: Enable verbose sampling only for debugging. Recorded enum mapping for hw_quant_profile must be kept stable; if new quant profiles are added, update normalization table to avoid card explosion.
